About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

The Role

You'll report to our General Counsel and own compliance and licensing at Plasma. That means building and running our global compliance program, and leading the licensing work that gets us into new markets.

This is a hands-on role. We're looking for an operator who's ready to own more. You'll set the priorities, write the docs yourself, work directly with partners and make sure things actually ship across Legal, Product and Engineering.

Global Compliance Program

  • Build and own the global program and proportionate market implementations: AML/CFT, sanctions, KYC and KYB, transaction monitoring across fiat and on-chain flows, Travel Rule and consumer protection. Make clear which controls Plasma operates and which sit with regulated partners.

  • Own the financial crime risk assessments, company-wide and for each market, and the policies and controls that follow from them.

  • Set the compliance conditions for new products, features and markets before launch, working with Product and Engineering from the design stage. Turn requirements into practical controls, identify owners and verify readiness, escalating material risks and unresolved legal questions to the General Counsel.

  • Own the compliance relationships with our banking, card and other regulated partners. Oversee the controls they require of us, the controls we rely on them for, and their diligence requests and audits.

  • Choose and run the compliance tooling with Operations and Engineering, and automate first-line review as volume grows, with clear escalation paths and quality checks.

  • Run compliance testing, staff training and independent audit readiness.

Global Licensing and Market Entry

  • Work alongside Legal in setting the licensing roadmap: which markets, which license in each, if needed, and in what order.

  • For each market, recommend whether to build, buy or partner, with the cost, timeline, capital and headcount each option needs, so Leadership can decide how to appropriately enter new markets.

  • Where needed, run licensing applications end to end: draft the regulatory business plan, program of operations and policies, coordinate financial projections with Finance and fit-and-proper filings with the relevant officers, and manage the regulator's questions through to approval.

  • Lead the regulatory side of acquiring licensed entities: diligence on the target's licenses and compliance record, change-in-control filings, and integration after closing.

  • Recommend when a product or market can run on a partner’s license and when it needs our own, working with Legal to resolve the regulatory perimeter. Document the agreed position for each product and turn it into clear launch conditions, so the reasoning holds up with regulators and partners.


Governance

  • Lead regulatory engagement for our licensing and compliance workstreams alongside Legal and the relevant local officers. Be Plasma's primary day-to-day contact for the compliance teams at our banking and card partners.

  • Report to Leadership on a regular cycle: license status, alerts and case backlog, suspicious activity filings, onboarding outcomes, open findings.

  • Track regulatory change in our markets and turn it into changes to the roadmap, the product and the program.

  • Work with Legal on regulatory analysis, outside counsel and consultants. Own the compliance and licensing budget within agreed priorities, and make the case for the people, tooling and specialist support needed to deliver.

  • Build the compliance and licensing function as Plasma grows, including recommending where to hire or use specialist support. Coordinate local officers and programs while preserving their jurisdiction-specific accountability and required independence.

The Bar

  • You have 4+ years in compliance, licensing or regulatory roles in payments, e-money, neobanking or digital assets firms. You have owned substantive workstreams at a fast-moving fintech and are ready to lead a function. We care more about what you have delivered than your previous title.

  • You have personally written and implemented meaningful parts of a compliance program, and can explain how you tested the controls and supported a regulator review or partner bank audit.

  • You have played a substantial hands-on role in a licensing application, regulatory approval or market-entry process. You can show what you drafted, which issues you resolved and how you drove it forward, not just which licenses your employer holds.

  • You have strong practical knowledge of AML, sanctions and KYC, with depth in at least one relevant regulatory framework and experience adapting controls for another market or working closely with local specialists.

  • You understand how responsibilities are divided between a fintech, its banking and card partners and its technology providers. You bring relevant experience in card programs, stablecoin on- and off-ramps or wallet models, and can get up to speed on the rest.

  • You take work from an open question to a clear recommendation and completed implementation. You write well, manage dependencies and influence cross-functional teams without relying on a large team beneath you. Previous people-management experience is helpful, not required.

Nice to have

  • You have run compliance for a card issuing program with a sponsor bank.

  • You have worked directly with UAE regulators (such as VARA, the CBUAE, ADGM or DIFC) or Asian regulators (such as MAS in Singapore or the SFC and HKMA in Hong Kong).

  • You hold a Law degree, CAMS or a similar certification.


What's in it for you

  • Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

  • A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

  • Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

  • Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

  • All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

  • Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

About Flowdesk

At Flowdesk, we are building the infrastructure powering the next era of global finance. As a full-service digital asset trading and technology firm, we provide liquidity solutions, OTC trading, and market infrastructure that connect digital assets to global markets with institutional-grade precision, transparency, and scale. Flowdesk combines expertise from traditional finance, algorithmic trading, and blockchain technology to deliver always-on trading capabilities across the digital asset ecosystem.

Founded in 2020, we are a global team supporting institutions, exchanges, and token issuers to enable a  tokenized financial markets ecosystem.

Why join Flowdesk? You’ll be joining a company operating at the intersection of finance, technology, and crypto; solving complex market problems, building critical infrastructure, and helping shape how digital assets connect to global liquidity. We move fast, think long term, and work with a strong ownership mindset across engineering, trading, product, operations, and business teams.

The opportunity

Flowdesk is expanding its regulated footprint. Alongside our MiCA authorization in Europe and our VARA broker-dealer license in the UAE, we are establishing a new US broker-dealer entity based in New York.

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to be the founding infrastructure engineer for this entity. You will design and build its technology platform from the ground up, to the standard expected of a US broker-dealer operating under SEC and FINRA oversight, while integrating it cleanly and securely with Flowdesk’s existing global infrastructure.

You will be part of the Infrastructure team, reporting to Flowdesk’s Lead of Infrastructure, and working day to day with the US broker-dealer leadership, Compliance, Risk, Engineering, Trading and Data teams.

Your mission will be to

Build the broker-dealer platform from the ground up

  • Design, build and document the entity’s infrastructure from day one: cloud accounts/projects, networking, identity and access management, environments and guardrails, all defined as code (Terraform, Ansible, etc).
  • Stand up Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows for the entity, including safe release strategies such as Blue/Green and Canary, and day-to-day operation.
  • Make clear, documented build-vs-reuse decisions: what should be shared with the Flowdesk group platform, and what must be segregated for the US entity.


Integrate with Flowdesk’s global infrastructure

  • Connect the broker-dealer securely to Flowdesk’s existing trading, data and platform services, including our Kubernetes operators, our in-house workload orchestrator built in Rust, and our internal tooling.
  • Define and implement the network, identity and data boundaries between the US entity and the wider group (private connectivity, segmentation, least-privilege access), so that integration never compromises regulatory separation.
  • Extend group-wide standards (observability, secrets management, CI/CD templates, internal tooling) to the US entity rather than reinventing them, and feed improvements back to the group platform.


Build for a regulated environment

  • Design infrastructure that supports the firm’s books-and-records obligations, including electronic recordkeeping under SEC Rule 17a-4 (immutable or audit-trail storage, retention, retrieval and the related cloud provider arrangements).
  • Implement the technical controls behind the firm’s cybersecurity and customer-information program, including centralised logging, incident detection, response and recovery capabilities aligned with the amended SEC Regulation S-P.
  • Build and regularly test backup, disaster recovery and failover for mission-critical systems, supporting the firm’s Business Continuity Plan.
  • Partner with Compliance and Risk to provide reliable, auditable infrastructure for risk controls, surveillance and regulatory reporting systems.
  • Own access reviews, change management and centralized logging so that every production change is traceable, and produce evidence for audits, regulatory exams and vendor due diligence.


Run and improve

  • Drive observability, reliability, performance tuning and FinOps across the entity’s stack.
  • Lead incident management and on-call for the broker-dealer, including post-incident reviews.
  • Manage relationships with infrastructure vendors (cloud, connectivity and other technology providers) and support third-party risk assessments.
  • Propose improvements, bring new ideas to the table, and help shape the US infrastructure function as the entity grows.

Requirements

Background and experience

  • 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform engineering, including at least one environment you built or substantially re-architected from scratch.
  • Experience in a regulated financial services environment, ideally a broker-dealer, exchange, FCM or trading firm, and familiarity with SEC/FINRA technology expectations (recordkeeping, business continuity, cybersecurity, change management).
  • Strong Kubernetes expertise, including Kubernetes operators.
  • Infrastructure as code with Terraform and/or Ansible on Google Cloud and/or AWS, including multi-account/multi-project setups, KMS, networking and IAM.
  • Substantial coding experience, plus Python for tooling and automation.
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD and GitOps.
  • Solid security fundamentals: secrets management, PKI/TLS, network segmentation, zero-trust access, log management.
  • Monitoring and observability experience.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical design to Compliance, auditors and non-technical stakeholders, backed by clear written documentation.
  • Strong ownership and autonomy: comfortable being the first infrastructure engineer for a new entity and prioritizing in a fast-moving build.


Nice to have

  • Experience with immutable/WORM storage (e.g. Object Lock, Bucket Lock) or external archiving solutions used for SEC Rule 17a-4.
  • Familiarity with digital asset infrastructure: MPC custody platforms, exchange connectivity, blockchain nodes, confidential computing.
  • Experience supporting a FINRA new membership application or a regulatory examination.
  • Exposure to control frameworks such as SOC 2 or NIST CSF.
  • Experience with low-latency or high-availability trading systems.

Join our team and help build the technical foundation of Flowdesk’s US broker-dealer: a resilient, compliant and cutting-edge platform that supports Flowdesk’s growth and innovation in digital asset markets!

Benefits

> International environment (English is the main language)

> 100% Coverage from Justworks Benefits (Medical, Dental, and Vision plans)

> Top of the range equipment, keyboard, laptop stand, 4K monitor & headphones

> Team events and offsites

The base salary range for this role is between $200,000 - $250,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

In this role, you would join Stripe's Vulnerability Management team, whose mission is to "Surface vulnerabilities at scale across Stripe." By joining our team, you will have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach, securely.

Our vision is to create a culture of continuous excellence in managing vulnerabilities. We want to enhance customer trust by giving users context about threats and vulnerabilities affecting Stripe's systems. We aim to be a key partner in Stripe's risk management by providing visibility into vulnerabilities across Stripe's products and services.

What you’ll do

You’ll build the systems that identify and prioritize vulnerabilities across Stripe’s codebases, production infrastructure, and employee laptops. These collect software bills of materials (SBOMs) across tens of millions of lines of code, scan hundreds of thousands of hosts for package and kernel versions, and connect that inventory to known vulnerabilities (CVEs).

You’ll also build agentic systems to investigate emerging threats. For example, parsing breaking security news, identifying the technologies involved, and determining whether Stripe is affected.

Alongside this engineering work, you’ll help teams across Stripe understand their exposure, prioritize fixes, and drive remediation. The role combines building data pipelines and security automation with hands-on vulnerability analysis and security guidance for partner teams.

Since our systems interact with the entire Stripe codebase, you'll work in Go, Java, Ruby, and Python. The services we own are written in Go, so most of your hands-on work will be in Go. The typical balance of hands-on work is about 70% coding and 30% reasoning about security issues or providing guidance to partner teams.

Responsibilities

  • Identify vulnerabilities using automated tools and triage them appropriately
  • Collaborate with other teams to drive remediation of vulnerabilities
  • Contribute to our overall security and risk management strategy
  • Continuously improve our security posture, processes, and tools

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of industry software engineering experience (does not include internships or co-ops)
  • Significant software engineering experience within the security domain
  • Empathy, strong communication skills and a deep respect for the power of collaboration
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • High standards for code quality and a constructive attitude to help others raise the bar
  • Have mentored early career engineers in security and software engineering craft

Preferred qualifications

  • An ability to think creatively and holistically about reducing risk in a complex environment
  • Familiarity with automated vulnerability identification tools and triage
  • Delivery of successful projects using agents to automate human review processes

About the position

We’re looking for compiler engineers to join a new ML Compilers Team at Jane Street. 

Machine learning is a critical pillar of our global business. Our ever-evolving trading environment serves as a unique, rapid-feedback platform for ML experimentation, allowing us to incorporate new ideas with relatively little friction. Our ML team is full of people with a shared love for the craft of software engineering, and for designing APIs and systems that are delightful to use.

ML compilers let us quickly turn research ideas and novel architectures into high-throughput training jobs and low-latency inference. To get the most out of our hardware resources and enable rapid model development and deployment, we are working to understand and improve the current ML compiler technologies and explore where it makes sense to build our own solutions. In this role, you would shape the development of our compiler stack.

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in.

About you

The ideal candidate has worked on an ML compiler in the past, but non-ML compiler experience is also valuable. Experience with any part of the stack is fine, be it high-level ML frameworks (PyTorch, Jax, TensorFlow), graph compilers (Inductor, XLA, TVM) or kernel DSLs (Triton, Helion, cuTile). You should understand how all those pieces fit together even if you are unfamiliar with specific parts. 

Some other things you might be excited about are:

  • Optimisations in ML compilers: algebraic rewriting, materialise vs recompute tradeoffs and fusion, equality saturation, scheduling languages, loop-level optimisation, autotuning
  • ML compiler frontends: graph capture, symbolic and dynamic shapes, control flow, automatic differentiation
  • GPU kernel programming and architecture: Triton, cuTile, CuTeDSL, CUDA, compute and memory hierarchies, programming with tensor cores
  • Compiler concepts: static analysis, intermediate representations like SSA and CFGs, instruction selection
  • ML inference: CUDA Graphs, KV caching, batching
  • ML training: Tensor/Sequence/Expert/Pipeline Parallelism, FSDP, NCCL, activation checkpointing
  • GPU debugging and optimisation: CUDA-GDB, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute
  • Formal methods: proof assistants, automated theorem provers, agentic proof systems
  • Programming languages and DSL design: embedded DSLs, staging and metaprogramming, type systems, functional programming
  • Fluency in English is required

If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com.

Who are we?

FalconX is a pioneering team of operators, investors, and builders committed to revolutionizing institutional access to the crypto markets. Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and  cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry's foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape.

Position Summary

FalconX is seeking a Personal Account Dealing Senior Compliance Associate to join our team and help to manage the program governing employee trading and conflicts of interest across the firm. In this role, you will review and adjudicate personal trading pre-clearance requests, monitor employee holdings and transactions for policy breaches, and administer the systems that make this program run. You will work at the intersection of compliance, data, and market structure — operating vendor-based employee compliance tooling alongside FalconX's internal systems to identify conflicts, detect undisclosed activity, and ensure the firm meets its code of ethics and market abuse obligations across the jurisdictions in which we operate.

Because FalconX operates in digital assets, this role extends the traditional personal account dealing discipline into self-custody wallets, on-chain activity, and token holdings. This role requires equal parts investigative rigor, technical comfort, and absolute discretion, and offers a unique opportunity to shape personal trading practice at one of the leading institutional digital asset platforms.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Pre-Clearance Adjudication: Independently review, approve, deny, or escalate employee pre-clearance requests for personal securities and digital asset transactions, applying restricted list rules, blackout periods, holding period requirements, and conflict checks within committed turnaround times.
  • Breach Identification & Escalation: Investigate suspected breaches of the personal account dealing policy — trading in restricted names, front-running firm or client activity, breach of minimum holding periods, use of undisclosed accounts — and prepare clear investigative narratives with supporting evidence for escalation to the Compliance Manager.
  • Restricted & Watch List Maintenance: Assist with maintaining the firm's restricted and watch lists, ensuring names and tokens are added and released on the correct triggers, and that list changes propagate correctly into the pre-clearance rule set.
  • MNPI Coordination: Work with Legal, Corporate Development, and business heads to ensure that material non-public information — deal activity, upcoming listings, client mandates — is reflected in trading restrictions on a timely basis.
  • Gifts & Entertainment / Outside Business Activities: Review and disposition gifts and entertainment and OBA submissions against firm thresholds, identify aggregation and pattern concerns, and escalate submissions raising bribery, inducement, or client-conflict risk.

Regulatory Compliance & Audit Support

  • Regulatory Alignment: Maintain a deep, up-to-date understanding of the personal trading and conflicts requirements applicable to the firm's regulated entities and their equivalents across jurisdictions, together with digital-asset-specific guidance, ensuring the program's coverage remains fully compliant as the regulatory perimeter shifts.
  • Policy Contribution: Partner with the Compliance Manager to update the personal account dealing policy, code of ethics, review playbooks, and standard operating procedures as regulations, product lines, and market structures evolve — with particular focus on where existing policy language does not cleanly address digital asset activity.
  • Audit Readiness: Assemble pre-clearance records, breach files, attestation completion evidence, and decision rationale for internal audit, bank partner reviews, and regulatory examinations, ensuring each file stands on its own without verbal explanation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Law, Data Science, or a related field.

Experience: 1–3 years of direct experience in personal account dealing, code of ethics, or employee compliance monitoring at a broker-dealer, asset manager, bank, proprietary trading firm, fintech, or digital asset platform. Experience running or administering a personal trading program — not solely submitting into one — is strongly preferred.

Platform Experience: Hands-on experience with STAR Compliance is strongly preferred, including administrator-level familiarity with pre-clearance rule configuration, broker and custodian data feeds, attestation campaigns, and reporting. Experience with comparable employee compliance platforms (ComplySci, MyComplianceOffice, Schwab Compliance Technologies) will be considered, provided the candidate has configured and maintained the system rather than only used its front end.

Analytical Mindset: Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to reconstruct what an employee actually traded from incomplete records, spot the account that was never disclosed, and distinguish a genuine oversight from a deliberate circumvention.

Discretion & Judgment: Proven ability to handle sensitive personal information about colleagues with complete confidentiality, and the composure to make and defend unpopular decisions — including denying a request from a senior stakeholder — without escalating unnecessarily or capitulating inappropriately.

Communication: Crisp verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to document decisions clearly, explain a denial in terms an employee understands, and articulate personal trading expectations to non-compliance stakeholders across the firm.

Digital Asset Interest: Genuine interest in digital asset markets and the practical mechanics of self-custody, on-chain activity, staking, and airdrops — enough to reason about how a policy written for equities should apply to a wallet.

Actual compensation for a successful candidate will be determined based on a number of factors such as location, skillset, experience, qualifications and the level at which the candidate is hired.
